experiments.hypothesis: E01b as committed (e566234): the reference for every gate.
The -42 dBFS gate is a microphone-gain assumption. Removing it (level judged only against the noise floor) makes behaviour identical at any gain; the risk is new stops on quiet sounds in quiet rooms.

Silero VAD alone as the speech-frame test (same 200 ms in 300 ms rule, same -42 dBFS gate): rejects non-speech (cough, laugh, horn, noise steps) and bridges stop closures, but cannot tell an acknowledgement from an interruption.
TEN VAD alone under the same conditions as B1 (10 ms hops, no extra buffering).
E01b acoustic frames with neural confirmation: a STOP also needs 100 ms of Silero speech in the window. Keeps E01b's fast onset and noise-floor logic; the VAD only vetoes non-speech.

The agent channel is a clean reference: caller frames whose level follows the agent's level at a fixed delay are echo, not a caller. Should remove the speakerphone false stops without hiding a caller who talks over the echo.
The same echo gate on E01b without any neural model (is the echo gate useful on its own?).

Gain-invariant loudness: compare the evidence with the caller's own earlier speech level instead of an absolute level. Evidence more than 6 dB below it is 'soft' and must last 1000 ms in 1400 ms before a STOP. Acknowledgements are short and soft; a soft but sustained interruption is still caught, later.
With a caller-relative reference in place the absolute -42 dBFS gate should no longer be needed.
